chapter: Kirby again, Garland gigs and later recordings
title: The interviewer's own record with Doc Cheatham and Holmes
summary: Vollmer recalls his 'More Blues and Jazz from Harlem' session with Cheatham, Bernhardt, Reuben Cole and Tommy Benford; Holmes says he was in poor shape.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: The title of the album was Blues and Jazz From Harlem. Because I know when I came to do my record, I had hooked up with Clyde at that time, and so I decided to build on that record and call my record More Blues and Jazz From Harlem. I remember my session had Doc Cheatham on trumpet, you on alto, Clyde on trombone, June Cole on piano...
That's right. That's who I couldn't think of his name.
That was Cozy Cole's younger brother, Reuben J. Cole, on piano. Bob Andrewwitz(?) we had on the tuba...
...and we had Tommy Benford on drums.
That's right. See how easy you name them all them off, just like that?
Well, that's because I remember. It was my first recording. And I was thrilled when you said you would...
When I see you fifty years from now, I want you to do the same thing.
I don't know if I can, but I was thrilled when you said you would do the recording for me, because I had always admired your playing...
I'm sorry I messed up the recording.
I don't think so at all.
I think so. Well, I was terrible shape then. I had no business playing at all. I couldn't think, you know what I mean. I was in bad shape. And when I hurt myself, then I said, "Well, this is it."
